Troops of the Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, have repelled successive attacks by terrorists on communities in Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State, while neutralising a suspected terrorist and recovering weapons and motorcycles in Kaduna State. The operations, conducted on November 14, 2026, also involved air support from the Air Component of Operation Fansan Yamma, which reportedly carried out multiple strikes against terrorists attempting to move a large herd of suspected rustled cattle away from the affected communities. The Acting Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, Capt Tamuno Sinivie, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday. Sinivie said troops of Sector 2 responded to attacks by motorcycle-riding terrorists on Wuya and Yarzabia communities in Anka LGA, engaging the assailants with superior firepower and forcing them to retreat. According to him, the terrorists regrouped and launched a second wave of attacks but were again repelled by the troops, who maintained their defensive positions. He said reinforcements later arrived and extended operations to neighbouring communities, while troops sustained aggressive patrols to prevent further attacks. Undeterred, the terrorists regrouped and launched a second wave of attacks, but were again decisively repelled by the troops,” the statement said. The military spokesman added that the Air Component deployed a combat aircraft to support ground troops during the operation. He said the aircraft identified terrorists attempting to move a large herd of suspected rustled cattle from the affected communities before engaging them in multiple air strikes. “The terrorists were subsequently engaged in multiple air strikes, neutralising scores of terrorists,” he stated. He said the troops encountered the suspects and engaged them in a gun battle, neutralising one terrorist while others escaped. A search of the area led to the recovery of two fabricated rifles, a mobile phone, substances suspected to be cannabis and other illicit drugs, as well as recharge cards. In another operation along the Buruku–Kaduna Road, the spokesman said troops engaged armed terrorists following intelligence about their movement. He said the terrorists fled into a nearby forest after being overwhelmed by the troops’ response, abandoning two motorcycles, which were subsequently recovered. “Troops continued pursuit and exploitation operations to deny the fleeing terrorists freedom of action,” he added. Sinivie said the operations demonstrated the determination of Operation Fansan Yamma to sustain pressure on terrorist groups, protect vulnerable communities and create a secure environment for farming and other socioeconomic activities across the North-West. He commended the troops for their resilience and fighting spirit, urging them to sustain the operational momentum. The military also called on residents to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing operations and restore lasting peace and security in the region.
